title: CKD-EPI 2021 eGFR
keywords: 2021 race-free equation removed the Black-race coefficient
for CKD diagnosis and staging use this, not Cockcroft-Gault
sources: Inker LA, et al. New Creatinine- and Cystatin C-Based Equations to Estimate GFR without Race. N Engl J Med. 2021;385(19):1737-1749.
National Kidney Foundation. CKD-EPI Creatinine Equation (2021).

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap (Content audit 2026-09-14, Batch 3), confirmed against the actual inventory: unlike Cockcroft-Gault (which turned out to already exist under Drug & Dosing — see that card's own changelog — and was cross-listed rather than duplicated), no CKD-EPI/eGFR calculator existed anywhere, only passing eGFR mentions in aki-staging-rrt/contrast-associated-aki/mehran-ci-akin-score. The race-free 2021 equation and its kappa/alpha constants (0.7/-0.241 female, 0.9/-0.302 male) WebSearch-verified against the NEJM derivation paper and the NKF's own published equation before building; hand-verified the resulting expression against two independent age/sex/creatinine test cases for a plausibility check before publishing.

purpose: Estimate glomerular filtration rate for CKD diagnosis and staging, using the current (2021) race-free CKD-EPI creatinine equation — the reference standard for staging, distinct from the existing cockcroft-gault card (Drug & Dosing, cross-listed here into Calculators too) which remains the standard most drug-dosing references are actually written against.
notes: This equation REMOVED the race coefficient present in the older 2009 CKD-EPI formula — do not apply any race adjustment on top of this result. For drug dosing specifically, check whether the drug's dosing reference was validated against Cockcroft-Gault (most older references) or eGFR (increasingly common in newer references) — they can give meaningfully different numbers in the same patient, especially at extremes of body size.

interpretation.label: G1 — normal or high (≥ 90)
interpretation.detail: Normal eGFR. CKD is only diagnosed at this stage if another marker of kidney damage is also present (proteinuria, structural abnormality, etc.) — eGFR alone doesn't diagnose G1 CKD.

interpretation.label: G2 — mildly decreased (60-89)
interpretation.detail: Same caveat as G1 — needs another marker of kidney damage to count as CKD at this stage.

interpretation.label: G3a — mildly-moderately decreased (45-59)
interpretation.detail: CKD by eGFR alone at this point. Screen for complications (anemia, mineral/bone disease); review nephrotoxic drugs and dosing.

interpretation.label: G3b — moderately-severely decreased (30-44)
interpretation.detail: Nephrology referral generally appropriate; renally-adjust drug dosing carefully.

interpretation.label: G4 — severely decreased (15-29)
interpretation.detail: Advanced CKD — renal-replacement-therapy planning territory; nephrology co-management.

interpretation.label: G5 — kidney failure (< 15)
interpretation.detail: Kidney failure — dialysis or transplant evaluation.

buildNote: Expression pre-resolves the sex-dependent kappa/alpha/female-multiplier terms into linear functions of a 0/1 sex select (kappa = 0.9 - 0.2*sex, alpha = -0.302 + 0.061*sex, femaleFactor = 1 + 0.012*sex) since the expression grammar has no conditional branching — same technique as the existing cockcroft-gault card's sex factor, extended to three coefficients that all depend on the same underlying select. Hand-verified: 50yo male, Scr 1.0 → ≈92 mL/min; 50yo female, Scr 0.8 → ≈90 mL/min, both in the expected range for a healthy adult of that age. Companion to cockcroft-gault (cross-listed here from Drug & Dosing) and meld-na — renal/hepatic estimating equations now cluster together in GI / Renal / Metabolic.
